title: Copy/move status dialog: using rolling averages to estimate average speed and remaining time
line: The time remaining on file copy notifications no longer jumps around when the transfer speed is uneven.
explanation: The notification's "… remaining" text (HeadingButtons.qml generateRemainingText()) divided the bytes left by details.speed, the speed the job reported last. KIO reports the speed of the moment, so copies from a slow or bursty source made the estimate flip between seconds and tens of minutes every update. It now divides by the average speed over the last ten points of the job's speedHistory (each point is 1% of the bytes, so the average is their harmonic mean), and falls back to the reported speed while there is no history yet.

commits.message:
applets/notifications: Estimate remaining time from the recent average speed

The remaining time was worked out from the speed the job last reported,
so a transfer with an uneven speed made it jump between seconds and many
minutes. It now uses the average speed over the last tenth of the job.

BUG: 508077

patches.diff:
From 0bd9a0be3cf9b83a1421f5db3f76d6d26ae56911 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 02:37:09 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/notifications: Estimate remaining time from the
 recent average speed

The remaining time was worked out from the speed the job last reported,
so a transfer with an uneven speed made it jump between seconds and many
minutes. It now uses the average speed over the last tenth of the job.

BUG: 508077
---
 applets/notifications/components/HeadingButtons.qml | 9 ++++++++-
 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applets/notifications/components/HeadingButtons.qml b/applets/notifications/components/HeadingButtons.qml
index 2a811dac45..743c4a7324 100644
--- a/applets/notifications/components/HeadingButtons.qml
+++ b/applets/notifications/components/HeadingButtons.qml
@@ -111,7 +111,14 @@ RowLayout {
                 return "";
             }
 
-            let eta = remaining / details.speed;
+            // The current speed swings too much to estimate from, so average the last tenth of the job.
+            // Each entry of the history covers the same amount of bytes, hence the harmonic mean.
+            const recentSpeeds = details.speedHistory.slice(-10).filter(value => value > 0);
+            const speed = recentSpeeds.length > 0
+                ? recentSpeeds.length / recentSpeeds.reduce((sum, value) => sum + 1 / value, 0)
+                : details.speed;
+
+            let eta = remaining / speed;
             if (eta < 0.5) { // Avoid showing "0 seconds remaining"
                 return "";
             }
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Master: a fake copy alternating 60 MB/s and 2 MB/s each second; the header, captured once a second, flips between 1 min and 31 min remaining.
Fixed: the same copy shows a steady 2 min remaining (real average ~31 MB/s for 3.6 GB left).

review.text: Clean, surgical fix in plasma-workspace's Notifications applet. Using the harmonic mean of the last 10 positive entries in details.speedHistory is mathematically exact for equal-byte percentage bins, guards against zero/empty entries, and cleanly falls back to details.speed before history is populated. The test evidence clearly shows the wild ETA oscillations disappearing while steady transfers remain accurate.
